P1.evidence: The setter was named and the handover acknowledged, but the notes were deliberately not read back — 'I've spoke to Kim... he briefed me in a little bit on your situation. However, I'm kind of old and old school. So, I would like to hear it from you.' That gets partial credit: the prospect knows he was discussed, but nothing was reflected to make him feel seen. The four-part frame never ran — 'what you want to achieve? And how can it actually help to get you there?' is two parts at most, with no 'where you are' and no 'what's in the way'. Agreement was taken with 'Cool?' and the open question landed cleanly.

P2.evidence: Five of nine ran well. Work was confirmed and qualified for desk time — 'Kim told me you work as a director in a security company that's correct' and later 'do you sit a lot during the day?'. Current training was asked directly ('Are you doing anything in terms of working out?'), diet was asked ('tell me more about nutrition. What does it look like right now?'), sleep was asked on both quantity and onset quality, and energy was asked and pursued into the afternoon crash. Against that, age came only because the prospect volunteered it ('now I'm 33'), height and weight were never asked, and the 40 lb figure is his own self-report. Most seriously, health conditions and injuries were never raised at any point in fifty-three minutes — no P2c, no P2d — on a prospect who is fully deconditioned and who volunteered a pending testosterone test that the rep did not follow up on. Results from current training were not asked either, though he was training almost nothing.

P3.evidence: The bridge question ran properly and did the heavy lifting — 'I understand you want to get in shape, but what would be your ultimate goal, your biggest why you want to do it?' — and produced the daughters, the example-setting and the presence-in-the-room material. But the rest of the ladder was climbed by the prospect rather than by the questions. The aesthetics/function fork, the mobility-strength-energy fork and 'something physical you want to do but can't' never ran. Crucially, 'when you're moving better, what does that actually do for you?' and 'who else does that impact?' were both replaced by the rep answering them himself — 'guys come in, they think they're just gonna fix their fitness level... but it turns out that after those six months, relationships got better, they got a raise' and the meeting-room story about the client who wanted to be the fittest man in the room. Telling a prospect his own why is not the same move as extracting it. The reflect-back arrived only as 'Checking the last box that's been missing', which is close but is not 'so this isn't really about the weight — it's about X, is that right?'.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase on the call and the strongest Phase 4 in this batch. Past attempts were opened well — 'you've been so athletic when you were younger. What happened that... kind of fell off during the journey?' — and then the rep picked the single most diagnostic thread and pulled it: 'So why did you actually fall off from those 10,000 steps a day? What happened?' That produced the real mechanism, that every streak was propped up by an external event and collapsed when the event ended. The prospect named the gap himself in his own words ('I don't have a structure. I think that's what I'm really missing') and the rep reinforced it correctly rather than arguing with it. Two things hold this short of a clean sweep: the 'one thing actually getting in the way' was never asked as a question, and the closing move was delivered as a diagnosis instead of a question — 'it's not an issue of lack of discipline, because you already done that before... if you can be successful at work, why shouldn't you be successful in the gym? What's stopping you, right?' The script wants the prospect to have to answer that, and here the rep answered it for him.

P5.evidence: The content of the consequence frame was present but it was narrated, not elicited. The rep delivered the two-year picture as a monologue — 'okay, so I'm going to start after vacation. Vacation ends, and then it gets busy... Then you realize, two years pass by, and you're in the same spot. I would even argue, like, you're not in the same spot. It's even worse, because we're getting older' — rather than asking 'if nothing changes, what does life look like over the next two years?'. Same with the line in the sand: the rep said it for him ('for you, this decision is about, okay, that's it. I'm drawing the line in the sand. I'm going to become Matthew 2.0') instead of asking whether he was ready to draw one. 'Is that something you're willing to settle for?' and 'Why not?' never ran at all, so the prospect never had to say out loud that the current trajectory is unacceptable. That is the missing load-bearing beam under the think-about-it forty minutes later.

P6.evidence: Well handled and correctly sequenced — the rep held the gate when the prospect asked for the price. 'How does the payment work?' was met with 'Yeah, let's go through that. Now, I need to ask you one crucial last question. If we can figure out all the logistics, all the details, and the payment, are you committed to actually showing up and doing the work to become that version 2.0 of Matthew, as we spoke about?' That is P6b almost verbatim, asked before any number. He got a real yes and tested it — 'tell me one thing that is great in your life that came as a result of being comfortable' — and the prospect confirmed under his own steam: 'the answer is yes. I'm no choice.' What did not run is P6a, the belief question. Nobody ever asked whether he believes he can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner — and belief in the provider, not commitment to the work, turned out to be the objection that killed the call.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted twice — the $6,000 present and then the $1,200 trial — so the phase applies. No step of it ran. No payment, no Trevor onboarding call scheduled or even described as a next action, no agreement email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire. The only thing scheduled was another sales call.

objection_plays.detail: Two moves ran and both were good. The pattern callback — 'you told me in the beginning that you've been putting this off time and time again. And this is happening again, man. And you know it.' — and the surfacing question, 'What's coming up? Be honest, be frank. There's only two of us.' A third, softer attempt followed: 'You really want me to give up on you that easily?' Everything else was skipped: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', and no 'that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now', which was sitting there ready given the Matthew 2.0 language the rep had already installed. The play was then abandoned on the prospect's second hold — 'I don't want to force you to anything. Let's do this. Let's follow up on Friday.'
No spouse or partner consult was raised. He referenced his wife only as someone he wants to keep comfortable, never as a decision input.

The isolate ran, correctly worded and correctly placed: 'apart from the, anything, What else would be stopping you from being 100% in on this?' Everything downstream was skipped. There was no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up — want to explore making it work?', and no permission question before touching money. Not one financial-picture item was asked: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. Instead the rep jumped the entire sequence and invented a $1,200 one-month entry unprompted. The isolate had already returned the answer that made the discount pointless — the prospect's blocker was a local alternative and an unknown provider, not capacity — and he confirmed it minutes later: 'even if you're like at $2,000 for six months, I still would have been like, okay, let me get my second opinion on this.'
No timing objection. The prospect argued the opposite — 'I'm for sure doing something. I have to do something. It's not necessarily like an option.'

The trigger is certainty-seeking about an unknown provider: 'I don't really know him. I've seen a couple videos' and 'I don't know if it would be better having someone more local and someone that I see that there's results'. The rep ran a recognisable version of the closing move — 'You can read all the testimonials, see your friend doing it, but until you actually start doing this and seeing yourself, you cannot say anything about whether it's going to work or not' — which is 'how will you know if you never actually try', and backed it with the guarantee. He never named the emotion ('would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?'), never used the bridge or the plane frame, and never asked what specifically he needed to see. The play was one third run.

Script gap, and the decisive one on this call. The prospect has a live, visible, working, cheaper substitute — a colleague he travels with who went from 400 lb to roughly 185 at 14% body fat under a local trainer at $600 a month with daily unannounced food checks. The playbook has no play for a functioning low-cost alternative, exactly the gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call. The rep's only response was to question the competing coach's kettlebell competence in general terms, which does not engage the proof the prospect can see with his own eyes. A second unscripted objection sits alongside it — remote-and-unknown versus local-and-verified — and got no response at all. Both are script gaps rather than rep failures, and both should be logged for the playbook rather than the coaching sheet.

notes: Phases 1 to 6 were the best work in this batch — real root cause, a genuine commitment yes before the number, and the price gate held when the prospect reached for it. It came apart at the objection stage: the isolate was asked and its answer was ignored, and the rep discounted to a $1,200 trial against an objection the prospect had already told him was not about money. Coach the sequence after the isolate, not the discovery before it.
